extracted.intended_audience: newsroom editors, journalists, media critics, and civic-minded readers
extracted.subtask_description: A concise set of editorial principles and front-page tests for newsroom decision‑making that prioritize civic stakes, accountability, clarity about falsehoods, and press‑freedom coverage. Intended to guide ledes, headlines, story selection, and framing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakes-based ledes
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakes-based ledes — start with what matters to the reader, not who said what
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open stories by foregrounding civic stakes, consequences, or what the audience needs to know instead of beginning with quotes, sourcing minutiae, or insider actions. Use ledes that tell a thoughtful citizen what they need to know immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language about lies
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain language about lies — call them lies, not "false claims"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit, direct language to characterize deliberate falsehoods rather than euphemisms. Avoid softeners that obscure intent or responsibility (e.g., prefer 'lies' over neutralizing phrases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headlines that don't sanewash
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines that don't sanewash — don't smooth incoherence into apparent reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write headlines that accurately reflect the article's most important fact and do not normalize or make incoherent or dangerous behavior seem reasonable. Avoid framing that sanitizes or legitimizes extreme or incoherent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist false equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Resist false equivalence — symmetric framing of asymmetric realities is a choice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid presenting two sides as equally valid when the evidence, facts, or power dynamics are markedly different. Contextualize disagreements instead of mechanically balancing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyper-local accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyper-local accountability — small papers' big watchdog work deserves elevation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize and amplify local watchdog reporting (e.g., prosecutions, local officials, election administrators) because it has direct civic consequences; don't overlook local beats in favor of purely national personality coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press freedom under threat
rubrics_metrics.description: Press freedom under threat — should be a recurring beat, not occasional
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover threats to press freedom consistently: lawsuits, legal pressures, administrative threats, and structural risks to journalism should be treated as ongoing coverage priorities, not one‑off items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-page test: Lede usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: "Would a thoughtful citizen learn what they need from this lede?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this question as an editorial litmus test for ledes—if the answer is no, revise to make civic utility and key facts clear up front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-page test: Headline accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Is the headline accurate to the article's most important fact?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure headlines align with and accurately represent the central fact or consequence in the piece; avoid clicky or misleading formulations that distort the article's main point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-page test: Euphemism check
rubrics_metrics.description: "Are we using euphemism that protects the powerful?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit language for euphemisms that shield powerful actors from accountability; replace protective phrasing with precise, descriptive terms that reflect responsibility and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-page test: Audience orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Are we covering this for journalists or for citizens?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize coverage decisions and story framing that serve citizens' information needs rather than insider-focused narratives that primarily interest other journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: Local prosecutors' decisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat prosecutorial choices as high-value civic reporting because they shape public safety and accountability; elevate such work above personality-driven national churn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: Election-administrator threats
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize reporting on threats to election administrators and electoral integrity, as these stories have direct democratic consequences and public-interest urgency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: Press-freedom lawsuits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give sustained attention to litigation and legal pressures that threaten journalism, documenting implications for reporting and democratic oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: Newsroom layoffs and civic cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsroom layoffs and their civic cost
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover newsroom staffing changes with an eye toward civic impact—how cuts affect reporting capacity, accountability, and the public's right to know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: Unreported testimony from House committees
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek out and amplify significant but underreported congressional testimony and records that have public‑interest implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: Personality-driven Beltway analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deprioritize coverage centered on personalities, insider drama, or horse‑race narratives that add little civic value or public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: Fluff that normalizes anti-democratic figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluff coverage that normalizes anti-democratic figures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid soft or humanizing features that serve to normalize actors who threaten democratic norms; resist coverage that diminishes the seriousness of anti‑democratic behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: Process stories with no substantive payoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Process stories with no substantive payoff
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publishing procedural or process‑focused pieces that do not yield meaningful information, accountability, or civic understanding for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overarching principle: Protecting democratic norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Sullivan's rubric is conservatism in the original sense: protecting earned democratic norms via diligent news judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt an editorial stance that treats journalism as civic stewardship—make choices that uphold democratic institutions, accountability, and the public's need for clear, consequential information.
